newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia govt sees competition between ports.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia govt sees competition between ports.

text.p: Australian Transport Minister John Sharp said on Monday Australian ports could compete with each other, despite their sparseness and limited cargo volumes.

".. while it is obvious that Australia lacks the close proximity of major ports in Western Europe, or cargo volumes of major hub ports like Singapore, there are plenty of opportunities to sharpen inter-port competition," Sharp said in a speech to a waterfront conference.
"The privatisation of Geelong and Portland, and possible future developments at Westernport, (all in the state of Victora) mean that Melbourne will not be able to be complacent," the minister said.
Kwinana, meanwhile, was close to Fremantle, the main Western Australian port for general cargo.

A standard-guage railway would help Brisbane, in Queensland, compete for cargo in the adjacent state of New South Wales while the two main New South Wales ports, Newcastle and Botany Bay (Sydney), competed with each other, he said.
"Progressive competition at the margin, and the possibility of effective competition, is crucial to ensuring that ports have the incentive to behave in an appropriate manner."
Sharp became Transport Minister when the Liberal-National government gained power in the March election.
A long-time opposition spokesman on transport, he has trenchantly criticized the former Labor government's failure to reform the waterfront, blaming its inaction on union influence.
Although Australia's ports improved their efficiency in the early 1990s, their position relative to international standards has slipped again over the past few years.
Sharp said in his speech that it cost A$4 to load a tonne of newsprint in New Zealand but A$19 to A$32 to unload it in Australia, depending on the port.
